title: NYC Daily Digest
text:
Good morning, Matthew ☕
Saturday, September 19, 2026

🌤️ Weather
NYC today: high ~72°F, low ~65°F. Mostly cloudy early, turning partly cloudy. No rain in the forecast. Winds light out of the east.
What to wear: light jacket or long sleeves — comfortable, easy day. Leave the umbrella home.

🗞️ Headlines
• House Republicans passed a 2026 budget bill 217–212; Democrats counter with a stopgap to fund the government through Oct 31.
• Trump says he's struck a deal with Denmark to expand the U.S. military footprint in Greenland.
• Russia holds parliamentary elections in illegally annexed regions of Ukraine — the first time it's done so there.
• Italian health officials link warmer, longer seasons to a wider spread of West Nile virus via mosquitoes.
• New study: regular reading boosts memory and executive function and helps slow brain aging in older adults.

🚇 Getting around
G line: through 5 a.m. Monday, Church Av–bound trains skip 4 Av–9 St, 15 St–Prospect Park, and Fort Hamilton Pkwy. Plan around it if you're in that stretch.

🎉 NYC today
• JapanFes on the Upper East Side — billed as the world's largest Japanese food festival.
• Feast of San Gennaro rolls on in Little Italy, marking its 100th year.
• David Byrne at Forest Hills Stadium (Queens) tonight, 7pm; Liz Phair + Sleater-Kinney at the Prospect Park bandshell.
• Smorgasburg (Williamsburg Sat) and the Transit Museum Bus Festival in Brooklyn Bridge Park, 10a–3:30p, free.

💡 Nugget
That reading study isn't just feel-good: consistent reading correlates with measurably better memory and slower cognitive aging. A few pages a day is one of the cheapest brain workouts going — a good excuse for a slow Saturday coffee-and-book morning.
